chapter: Maple Leaf, own orchestra and rivals
title: Who played in Perez's band; Bocage and Sidney Bechet
summary: Charles substituted for Perez now and then and names his sidemen; they discuss Eagle band clarinetists.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: I just wondered if you knew him or not, because he's the one that talked about it. He really lived that life, you know. He was one of them. And we never did find out who played in Perez's band. You said you substituted for Perez when he couldn't make it your good.
Yeah, now. Because I had my own, you see. Oh, I see. Well, who would be in Perez's band?
Well, he had, let me see, Jimmy Brown, Big Island, George Field, George Backett. Now and then, when Louis left, George Backett. And do you remember George Field?
I never knew him. He moved up to Chicago before my time. That's right.
But he's in, George Backett, you ever knew him?
No, he came back and died and I just missed him. He died just before I got to New Orleans.
Is that so? Well, he was a good clarinet player too.
I heard him on record, you know, with this fellow, they called him Whining Boy, Jelly Roll Martin?
No, just, Boccai was at it. Paul Barnes, Bolo was playing sax on some of the same records. Sidney Bashe, you heard him? Plenty. I met him once.
Well Sidney Bashe was the clarinet player with them. With which? With the Eagle band. Oh yeah. That was his band. That's right.
He and Johnny Dodds, huh, both? They had a good line up. But tough music. No, he didn't know no music. I say it was strictly tongue, tongue-style.

That's right. Just what they could pick up. They made their own. In other words, they'd hear a piano copy there, and they'd go there and compose it to suit themselves. And they really made well with it too.
